findings.text: §6 gives `check_all_tools` an interpreter floor while `PythonVersion.meets_minimum`/`MIN_PYTHON` in `imas_codex/remote/python.py:43,66` is the existing floor primitive and `get_python_status` is already wired into `tools status`; adding a parallel floor yields two places that decide whether the remote interpreter is acceptable

findings.reason: citing the existing owner turns §6 from a new probe into an extension plus one clearly-scoped gap (module-loaded interpreters), which is the honest change.
findings.text: §6 names `DataSystemBase`, `data_access_patterns` and `check_all_tools` as the machinery it consolidates but never opens `imas_codex/remote/python.py`, the module that owns remote interpreter detection and the floor; a reviewer running the reuse map finds an owner the plan did not cite

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §6 hides the facility block, the merge with a data system's own keys and the pass-down to the executor behind one resolver in `imas_codex/remote/tools.py`; §3 hides the dynamic-page rule, the `fronts_database` mark and the PID group behind the existing `WikiChunk-[:DOCUMENTS]->FacilitySignal` linkage rather than spreading new surface across owners.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §6 adds an interpreter floor to `check_all_tools` beside the existing floor owner `imas_codex/remote/python.py`, and `imas-codex tools status` (imas_codex/cli/tools.py:76-84) already reports Python status from `get_python_status` alongside `check_all_tools`, so the plan creates a second interpreter-version mechanism on the same surface instead of naming the one to extend.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; no section adds to any of the four families. §6 accounts in its own text ("no new CLI command is added"; the interpreter floor and importability ride the existing `missing_required` / `version_too_old` verdicts of `check_tool`/`check_all_tools`), §2's additions are FacilitySignal schema slots rather than Python definitions or MCP views, and §3's `fronts_database` is a graph property reusing the existing edge.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §6 proposes a remote-interpreter floor without citing `imas_codex/remote/python.py`, which already owns remote Python detection (`get_python_status`) and the version-floor primitive (`PythonVersion.meets_minimum`, `MIN_PYTHON`); the plan searched the facility-config and tools-probe machinery but not the module that would carry its floor.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §6 is a consolidation, not a thin layer: it retires `data_access_patterns.setup_commands` (a key that `tcv.yaml:271` sets and no code reads — confirmed by rg over `imas_codex/`, which reads only `key_tools`, `code_import_patterns`, `independent_trees` and `primary_method` from that map) and keeps `DataSystemBase` keys with the single stated override role, so the section justifies the merge in its own text.
